Shorter Term or Lower Payment?

After a partial settlement, your bank can either keep your payment and shorten the mortgage, or keep the end date and lower your payment. Keeping the payment usually saves more interest. Lowering it gives you more cash each month.

Example: AED 1,200,000 at 5.50% with 20 years left, an AED 200,000 partial settlement and an AED 2,000 fee. Keeping the payment at AED 8,255 finishes the mortgage 62 months early and saves AED 316,542 after the fee. Lowering the payment to AED 6,879 saves AED 128,186.

How to Use This Calculator

  1. Enter your outstanding balance, rate and remaining term from your latest statement
  2. Add a lump sum, a monthly extra payment or both
  3. Enter the fee your bank quotes. A prompt shows the 1% cap for your balance
  4. Compare the net saving and new payment under each option

The calculation assumes your rate stays the same. Most UAE mortgages become variable after a fixed period, so treat the saving as an estimate.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the fee for partial settlement of a UAE mortgage?
A 2019 Central Bank of the UAE circular capped early or partial settlement fees on home loans at 1% of the outstanding balance or AED 10,000, whichever is lower. Banks can charge less, and some allow a free amount each year, so check your contract.
Should I shorten my mortgage term or lower my payment?
Shortening the term usually saves more interest, because you keep repaying at the higher amount. Lowering the payment leaves more cash free each month. Check which options your bank offers, since some apply a part-payment one way by default.
Is it worth paying off a mortgage early in the UAE?
It depends on your rate and the alternatives. There is no income tax in the UAE to offset mortgage interest, so the saving is simple, but investments may earn more with more risk. Keep an emergency fund, particularly as an expat whose residency may depend on employment.
Does the fee apply if I pay off the whole mortgage?
Full settlement usually carries the same capped fee, and you may also pay to release the mortgage at the land department. Ask your bank for a settlement letter that sets out the amounts.
